Carbon vs Aluminium: Is it worth the extra money?

My opinion on the subject is that carbon just isn't worth it for the vast majority of riders. It's too damn expensive and the difference is negligible unless you're regularly racing against strong competitors, and that is obviously not something a normal cyclist does. Not only that, but carbon bikes simply can't handle crashes or falls as well. edit: They can also be more delicate to work with during maintenance. Take special care when tightening or loosening bolts and always use a torque wrench.

Bikes in general normally cost way more than they should, which is what makes cheaper lower quality department store bikes so appealing. Most bikes are made in assembly lines in places like china and taiwan for pennies on the dollar and are marked waaaaaay up by the time they get to shops. It's practically a crime. Carbon is a more advanced material to work with of course, but the huge price increase is definitely not justified in my opinion.

Regarding durability in a crash, I should probably add that in my opinion, an ordinary cyclist shouldn't really be putting themselves in situation where they are going to crash in the first place. Granted, in rare cases it may be beyond your control. In the nearly 2 years that I've been cycling almost daily and in all kinds of weather from summer heat to heavy rain and even during snowfall, I've only crashed once, and that was in my first month. It was because I was ignorant of the fact that railroad tracks should be crossed perpendicularly. My front tire got wedged in the groove, and I flew off the bike. I ended up with a bruised leg and a derailed chain, but thanks to my helmet I was fine. My cheap steel bike was also totally fine. That said, I've encountered riders who have been riding a lot longer but who ride less often than me, and some of them seem to have a knack for crashing. I think they are probably not being as cautious as I am. For people like that, I wouldn't recommend a carbon bike. But I would recommend a helmet.

So is carbon worth the money? No. Definitely not. What do you think?
